title: U.S. House · New York's 1st Congressional District
area: Eastern Long Island, covering all of Suffolk County east of Smithtown/Islip (the North and South Forks, the Hamptons, and the Suffolk suburbs including Amityville and Babylon).

context.text: Incumbent Nicholas LaLota advanced without a primary after the Republican and Conservative Party primaries were canceled. Christopher Gallant won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Lukas Ventouras, 62.9% to 37.0%. As of September 22, 2026, Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rated the general election "Solid Republican," Decision Desk rated it "Lean Republican," and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated it "Likely Republican."
Two independent candidates, Jordan Maggio and Thomas Sorensen, withdrew or were disqualified and are not on the November ballot.

summary.text: Nicholas J. LaLota is the Republican and Conservative Party incumbent for New York's 1st District, first elected in 2022 and sworn in in January 2023. A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Navy veteran, he held local and county government posts on Long Island, including Amityville village trustee and Suffolk County elections commissioner, before running for Congress. He serves on the Appropriations, Homeland Security, and Small Business committees.

background.text: Born in Bethpage, New York, and lives in Amityville; his official biography says his father was a Nassau County police officer and his stepfather served in the Navy.
Graduated from St. Anthony's High School, then earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Naval Academy in Annapolis (2000).

Served in the U.S. Navy from 1996 to 2007 as a Surface Warfare Officer, attaining the rank of Lieutenant; his official biography says he deployed overseas three times, served aboard the USS Curts and the USS Carl Vinson, and received a Joint Service Commendation Medal.
Earned an MBA from Hofstra University (2012) and a law degree from Hofstra University (2020).
Appointed to the Amityville Board of Trustees in 2013 and elected in 2014 and re-elected in 2015; his official biography says he served as the village's budget officer.

Since 2008, held local-government roles on Long Island, including chief of staff to a New York State Senator, Commissioner of the Suffolk County Board of Elections (his official biography says he was the youngest person to hold the post in three decades), and chief of staff to the Suffolk County Legislature.
Won the open 1st District seat in the November 2022 general election, defeating Bridget M. Fleming, 55.5% to 44.5%; re-elected in 2024 over John Avlon, 55.2% to 44.8%.

In 2025-2026, serves on the Appropriations Committee (Vice Chair of the Financial Services and General Government Subcommittee), the Homeland Security Committee, and the Small Business Committee (Chair of the Contracting and Infrastructure Subcommittee).
According to his official biography, he is married to Kaylie and they are raising three daughters.

priorities.text: Describes his focus as border security and opposing New York's sanctuary-city policies, restoring the SALT deduction, and reducing federal spending while protecting Social Security, Medicare, and veterans' health care.
Cites membership in the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus and For Country Caucus as reflecting a preference for cross-party solutions over partisanship.

positions.summary: In a January 2026 statement he said he voted to extend the enhanced ACA premium tax credits for three years, while calling the ACA deeply flawed and wanting income caps reinstated.
positions.quote: While the ACA is deeply flawed, I voted to extend the Enhanced Premium Tax Credits for three years to help the nearly 50,000 constituents who rely on them

record.text: Serves on the House Appropriations Committee (Vice Chair, Financial Services and General Government Subcommittee) and the House Small Business Committee (Chairman, Contracting and Infrastructure Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the House Homeland Security Committee and House Armed Services Committee in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

summary.text: Christopher Gallant is the Democratic nominee in New York's 1st District. Born in Smithtown, he enlisted in the Army at 17, worked as an air traffic controller, and now flies Black Hawk helicopters in the New York Army National Guard; he is also a volunteer firefighter and a former local air traffic controllers' union president. He won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with about 63% of the vote and describes his campaign as focused on affordability, health care and veterans' benefits, and restoring trust in government.

background.text: Born in Smithtown, New York; lives in Amity Harbor, which is outside the 1st District, and has said he would not move into the district if elected.
Enlisted in the Army at age 17 and trained as an air traffic controller; deployed to Kuwait in 2012.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Dowling College in 2014; the VoteVets profile describes his degree as one in Aviation Management.
Worked as an FAA air traffic controller, most recently at Kennedy Airport, and served as local president of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association.

Became a Black Hawk pilot in the New York Army National Guard; according to the VoteVets profile, his service has included directing emergency operations at the Javits Center during the COVID-19 pandemic and air support for the Secret Service during presidential campaigns, and he deployed again in 2022. He also served as an Equal Opportunity representative in the U.S. Army.

Volunteer firefighter with the Copiague Fire Department and affiliated with the Veterans of Foreign Wars (a post leader, per Politics NY), the American Legion, and the Army Aviation Association of America, among other organizations.
Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Lukas Ventouras, 62.9% to 37.0%.

priorities.text: Says his campaign focuses on affordability (housing, groceries, energy), protecting Medicare, Social Security, and veterans' benefits, and defending voting rights and reproductive freedom.
priorities.quote: Tackle affordability, from housing to groceries to energy, so Long Island families can build stable, secure lives without being priced out of the communities they love.

priorities.text: Says his priorities include affordable housing, education, health care access, fair wages, veterans' benefits, and government accountability.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to protect reproductive freedom.
positions.quote: I'll fight to protect voting rights, reproductive freedom, and the rule of law

positions.summary: Campaign site's health care plan lists expanding Medicare to cover dental, hearing and vision care.
positions.quote: Expand Medicare to cover dental, hearing, and vision care.

statements.quote: Secure federal housing grants to increase workforce housing, starter homes, and attainable housing options for young professionals, first responders, teachers, nurses, veterans, and working families.
statements.context: On his campaign site (Mission One action plan)

statements.quote: Push for affordable childcare tax incentives so parents are not forced to choose between their careers and caring for their children.
